headline: High: shared writable state and broad egress make cross-agent leakage and action conflicts plausible by default; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application-defined files and uses shared checkpointer state; marketingskills also reads/writes skill files and shared context. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through shared files or persisted state, even though no direct parser bridge is documented. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or checkpointer store
IF either agent treats file contents or persisted state as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces and checkpointer namespaces
Add provenance tags to shared state entries
Require explicit allowlists for files each agent may read
Insert a human review step before executing instructions found in files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and LangGraph has broad network egress while marketingskills can call GitHub and marketing-skills.com. If they share a workspace, sensitive graph state or marketing context can flow into outbound requests or outputs. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or checkpointer-backed state
IF either agent sends file contents or shared context into outbound API calls
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and workspaces
Disable outbound calls for one agent during sensitive runs
Redact secrets before writing shared state
Restrict network destinations with an allowlist
requires-engineering: add per-field data-class filtering before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem and spawn_subprocesses, and LangGraph explicitly supports shared state via a checkpointer store. If they operate on the same directory or mutable state, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt artifacts. Because the profiles show default write capability and shared-state support, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or shared store
IF no external locking or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Turn off one agent's write path for shared resources
Snapshot state before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can pass outputs between nodes, while marketingskills is built from shared context and skill references. That makes it plausible that one agent's output becomes the other's input without verification. The profiles do not show autonomous downstream actions like email sending, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes marketingskills output into a downstream node without validation
IF the downstream node acts on marketing claims as authoritative
mitigations: Add a verification node between agents
Require citations for factual claims before reuse
Limit downstream actions to draft-only mode
Log and review handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on inter-agent messages

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class, residency mismatch, or certification gap is documented in either profile. LangGraph handles model provider API keys and marketingskills touches marketing content, so a compliance issue is possible only if the operator routes regulated data through them. With no direct mismatch evidence, low is the appropriate conservative severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are routed through either agent
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention and deletion settings
Use separate storage for marketing and operational data
Review vendor and hosting locations before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
